chunks: What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from Zurārah and Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Together we asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who had intercourse with his wife in the month of Ramaḍān, and had intercourse with his wife while he was in iḥrām, and he saw that as nothing but lawful for him. He said: There is nothing upon him.

key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, the time of obligatory sawm (fasting)
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: no liability, penalty, or expiation is due upon him
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of iḥrām for hajj or ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who has intercourse in Ramaḍān or while in iḥrām thinking it is lawful?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام concerning a man who had intercourse during Ramaḍān and while in iḥrām, believing that such conduct was lawful for him. The Imam عليه السلام states that nothing is upon him, indicating the legal effect of acting in ignorance of the prohibition.
